comparison: Both strongly support the core transgenerational inheritance findings (C26-C30, C84-C85). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and experimental design details, while peer reviewers focus on independent validation and robustness. Peer review also includes attenuation claims (C2, C3, C37, C38) that OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Both support the attenuation pattern in F1/F2 generations (C2, C3, C37, C38). OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification, while peer reviewers incorporate these claims into their broader affirmation of the transgenerational inheritance findings without separate discussion of attenuation.

Both strongly support this as an independent replication study (C4, C31). OpenEval emphasizes methodological alignment with Murphy lab protocols and appropriate citations. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight the importance of independent confirmation and reproducibility across laboratories.

Both support the authors' implementation of Murphy lab protocols including sodium azide use (C22, C52, C55, C56). OpenEval details the optimization process (400 mM vs 1 M), while peer reviewers confirm the authors followed standard protocols and appreciate methodological transparency.

Both support the critical role of sodium azide in detecting transgenerational inheritance (C17-C19). OpenEval cites Kaletsky et al. 2025 and connects to Hunter group's negative results. Peer reviewers extensively discuss how procedural differences (azide vs no azide) explain discrepancies between Murphy and Hunter groups (C20, C21).

Perfect agreement on accurately representing Hunter group's negative findings (C5, C15, C16, C32). Both evaluations confirm appropriate citation and contextualization of conflicting prior work. OpenEval notes this provides context for the replication study, while peer reviewers discuss it extensively in relation to methodological differences.

Both support the authors' conclusions about methodological sensitivity explaining discrepancies (C33-C36). OpenEval emphasizes well-documented controls and reasonable inference from sodium azide findings. Peer reviewers accept the interpretation about media ingredients and procedural differences, noting data robustness.

Both address conclusions about protocol variations (C20, C21). OpenEval groups these with broader methodological conclusions (C33-C36), while peer reviewers specifically discuss how procedural differences explain the Hunter group's inability to observe transgenerational effects.

Perfect agreement on the study's rationale and focus on F2 persistence (C23-C25). OpenEval notes consistency with literature context and experimental design. Peer reviewers confirm the focus is appropriate given Murphy lab reported multi-generational effects while Hunter group only observed F1.

Perfect agreement on experimental design quality (C60-C72). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of biological independence, replication adequacy, and sample sizes. Peer reviewers affirm robustness with 4 trials and note methods are clearly outlined for reproducibility.

Perfect agreement on statistical methods (C76-C81). OpenEval details appropriate assumption testing and transparent outlier handling. Peer reviewers implicitly accept statistical approach by describing data as robust and not raising concerns about analytical methods.

Contrasting evaluations of the media preparation modification (C44-C47). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to deviation from Murphy protocol without validation data, noting potential impact on comparability. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing it as acceptable methodological detail and appreciating transparency about reagent sources.

Strong agreement on standard methods (C39-C43, C48-C51, C53, C57-C59, C73-C75, C82). OpenEval confirms appropriate citations and sufficient detail for replication. Peer reviewers affirm methods are clearly outlined and following Murphy lab protocol. Peer review also includes C83 and C86 not in OpenEval's grouping.

Both support background claims about C. elegans biology and behavior (C6-C10). OpenEval confirms appropriate citations to established literature. Peer reviewers do not question these claims and affirm the broader context. Peer review also includes C1, C11-C14 in their background evaluation.

Both support mechanistic background claims (C12-C14). OpenEval confirms appropriate attribution to prior work (Cecere 2021, Sengupta et al. 2024). Peer reviewers include these in their broader acceptance of background literature without specific discussion.
